free.title: Islands in the Park: A Caribbean Jam
free.caption:
FREE · PROSPECT PARK · SUN SEP 6

Carnival weekend gets a free Sunday encore: Islands in the Park, a Caribbean jam taking over Smorgasburg at Breeze Hill in Prospect Park, 11AM to 6PM.

Smorgasburg and I Am CaribBeing are running it together, so the vendor row leans all the way in. Guest chef Scotley Innis is on jerk chicken, Wah Gwaan and Tanty Darlene's Kitchen are serving, and there is live steel pan plus DJ sets going most of the afternoon. There is an all ages arts and crafts setup too, which makes this one of the rare food festivals that actually works with kids in tow.

Entry is free. Come in from the Lincoln Road side off the B, Q or S at Prospect Park and the hill is a short walk along the lake.

Tip: eat before 1PM. The jerk line and the shady spots both disappear at the same time.

Save this and send it to whoever you want on the grass with you.

food.title: Zabar's on a Sunday
food.caption:
FOOD · UPPER WEST SIDE

The best cheap Sunday in NYC food is not a restaurant. It is the counter at Zabar's, 2245 Broadway at 80th, open 9AM to 6PM on Sundays and running since 1934.

You take a ticket, you wait with everyone else, and someone hand slices smoked salmon in front of you to whatever thickness you ask for. That is the whole ritual. Around it there is a cheese and olive wall the regulars hit first, a coffee counter, and a mezzanine floor of kitchenware that most visitors never notice is up there.

Browsing costs nothing, which is why locals treat it as a walk rather than an errand. The cafe on the corner keeps the same Sunday hours if you want to eat on the spot instead.

Tip: ask for a taste before you commit to a half pound. They expect it.

Save this for the next Sunday you were going to wait ninety minutes for brunch.

art.title: 6 SECRETS OF ROCKEFELLER CENTER
art.caption:
HIDDEN GEM · ROCKEFELLER CENTER

Six things hiding in plain sight at Rockefeller Center, the free Midtown walk most New Yorkers only do when someone visits.

The Channel Gardens are named for the English Channel because they run between the British and French buildings. The land under all of it was once the Elgin Botanic Garden, the first public botanical garden in the United States. And the corner at 49th and Sixth stayed put because the owner refused to sell, so the complex was simply built around him.

Three more you cannot walk into. There is a full rooftop garden above Radio City Music Hall. Inside Radio City there is a private Art Deco apartment with gold leaf ceilings, built for the showman it is nicknamed after. And the famous 1932 photo of workers eating lunch on a beam was staged on the 69th floor to promote the building.

Tip: go before 9AM. It is the only hour the plaza belongs to the people who live here.

Save this and send it to whoever says Midtown is boring.
